3.1.1.1 
Purpose 
The Project Steering Committee (TuLePSC) acts as a governance body by providing high level 
oversight of the strategic direction and management of the Tuvalu Learning Project (TuLeP). 
TuLePSC meetings provide a forum for strategic issues to be discussed and decisions made 
on the overall direction of the Project. The TuLePSC meetings provide opportunities for the 
examination of annual work plans and budgets and the provision of strategic advice on the 
allocation of resources by the Project.

MANAGEMENT STATEMENT 
 
 
MANAGEMENT STATEMENT 
 
It is with great pleasure that the Ministry of Finance presents these Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). Our 
SOPs are in two volumes: 
◼ Volume I describes the operating procedures of the CPMO (the Ministry’s Central Project Management 
Office) 
◼ Volume II describes standard operating procedures for Project Management Units across the 
Government in terms of financial management, procurement, environmental and social safeguards and 
monitoring and evaluation 
The Government of Tuvalu has been and will continue to implement a significant number of strategic, high 
priority development projects, with the financial and technical assistance of the World Bank. These Government 
projects are essential to develop our economy, to protect our environment, to build our human capital and to 
provide the social services our people need.  
The CPMO exists to support these development projects in terms of project management (financial 
management, procurement, environmental and social safeguards and M&E). Being a small country, it was 
essential that we established the CPMO as a high-profile central unit, in order to realize economies of scale, to 
build the capacities of project implementers, and to standardize the methods and procedures used by all our 
Government project implementers. The CPMO is thus an essential player in promoting and encouraging sound 
project management and in ensuring our strategic, national projects are implemented smoothly and effectively. 
These procedures aim to assist our project management units (PMUs) to better practice financial management, 
procurement, environmental and social safeguards and monitoring and evaluation. They establish the 
objectives, processes, good practice standards, and templates in each of these four areas. The CPMO will 
support our PMUs to implement the procedures defined in this Volume. 
Future projects will able to adopt these procedures, as a template, in their own SOPs agreed with the World 
Bank, thus saving significant time and effort, encouraging a common approach and avoiding duplication.  
This document therefore lays the foundations for the Government of Tuvalu to ensure its strategic development 
projects are well managed, are efficient and are effective in generating the development results our nation 
depends upon.  
 
 
 
--------------------------------------- 
Mr Niuatui Niuatui 
Acting Secretary for Ministry of Finance 
 
 
Date: -----------------------------

The Executive – The Government of Tuvalu Executive branch includes the British Monarch as Head of State represented by the Governor General who is appointed on the advice of the Prime Minister in consultation with Members of Parliament. Cabinet is appointed by the Governor General on the recommendation of the Prime Minister who is chosen by the elected members of Parliament. The current Cabinet comprises the Prime Minister, Deputy Prime Minister and four Ministers. The Prime Minister and the Deputy Prime Minister are elected by the Members of Parliament. The Attorney General, the principal legal adviser to the Government, in accordance with s.79 of the Constitution and Rule 50 of the Rules of Procedure, attends Cabinet and all sittings of Parliament and its committees, is allowed to take part in proceedings but is not entitled to vote.
